### Observed differences

- In the later window, A06 appears in about 31 in 100 traces (61 of 200) versus about 7 in 100 (13 of 200) before, and it still almost never repeats within a case (mean occurrences per trace 0.31 versus 0.065). [OCC001]
- A06's behaviour changed in routing and placement as well: in the later window about 85 in 100 of its observed outgoing transitions go to A16, whereas before (only 13 observed transitions) they were spread over roughly ten targets with none above about 15 in 100; A06 also sits much earlier in the trace (mean event position about 0.25 versus about 0.67). [DIR001, POS001]
- A new connection into A06 appears: A15 now sends about 15 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A06 (before, none were observed), and the short sequences A15→A06 and A06→A16 — seen in only 1–2 traces before — now appear in about 52 and 54 of 200 traces, with A06→A16 almost always immediately consecutive. [DIR002, LAG001, LAG004]
- A06 now precedes A27, A28, A29, A33 and A46 in about 27–29 in 100 traces; before, it more often followed them (about 5 in 100), with co-occurrence up from about 7 to about 31 in 100 traces. A06 also appears without A19 or without A25 in about 21–25 in 100 later traces (about 4–5 in 100 before). [REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- A19, A20, A25 and A26 rerouted: before, their outgoing transitions split between A33 (about 41–54 in 100) and A29 (about 43–59 in 100); in the later window about 92–98 in 100 go to A27, and all four run earlier (mean event position about 0.33 versus about 0.60). The previously common short-distance links from A19 and A25 into A29/A33 now show up in only about 1 of 200 traces each. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, LAG010, LAG011, LAG012]
- A46 moved the other way: before, about 95 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went straight to A27; in the later window they spread across A25 (about 29 in 100), A26 (about 23), A19 (about 22) and A20 (about 22), and A46→A27, when it occurs, now typically sits two events away rather than one. [DIR009, LAG018]
- A28 and A29 became near-deterministic steps: A28's outgoing transitions go to A29 in about 98 in 100 cases (before about 50) and A29's go to A33 in about 99 in 100 (before about 48), both almost always at distance 1 in the later window. [DIR007, DIR008, LAG015, LAG017]
- The order of the block flipped: before, A27 and A28 preceded A19/A20/A25/A26 in about 22–27 in 100 traces; in the later window, A19/A20/A25/A26 precede A27/A28 in about 21–31 in 100 traces and the reverse order has nearly disappeared, while A27, A28 and A29 themselves sit slightly later (mean event position up about 0.03–0.04). [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, POS006, POS007, POS008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that routing and ordering around the A27/A28/A29/A33 block were restructured, and that A06 took on a new, much more frequent early role. In the later window, A19, A20, A25 and A26 lead almost exclusively to A27 instead of branching between A29 and A33; A46 feeds into A19/A20/A25/A26 instead of running straight to A27; A28 and A29 behave as near-fixed consecutive steps into A33; and A06 — previously rare (about 7 in 100 traces) and late — now occurs in about 3 in 10 traces, early, after A15 and before A16, and ahead of A27/A28/A29/A33/A46. The flipped ordering between the A19/A20/A25/A26 group and A27/A28 is shown directly by the relation and event-distance evidence, not by position shifts alone. [DIR003, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, REL010, REL017, LAG001, LAG004, LAG015]

The support is direct and consistent: successor profiles, pairwise relations, event distances and positions all point to the same rerouting, and 53 qualifying items is many times the 0.78 expected by chance when screening 156 units, so the pattern as a whole is not what random re-splits of unchanged behaviour typically produce. [OCC001, DIR001, REL005, LAG001]

Limitations remain: several items describe one underlying trace behaviour — the A06 items (occurrence, direction, position, relations, distances) overlap heavily, as do the four rerouted activities — so they are not independent confirmations, and a few later-window profiles rest on only 1–2 observations. An important competing explanation cannot be ruled out: a shift in the mix of pre-existing variants, for example a variant that already contained A06 and the A46→A19/A20/A25/A26→A27 routing simply being sampled more often in the later window, would produce the same differences without any structural change. [LAG010, LAG011, LAG012, OCC001, DIR009]
